newsitem.title: USA: Widow gets newly minted Jackie Robinson coins.
newsitem.headline: Widow gets newly minted Jackie Robinson coins.

text.p: Fifty years after he broke the colour barrier to join the Brooklyn Dodgers, Jackie Robinson became the first black American to be honoured on a gold commemorative U.S. coin.
At a ceremony outdoors at the Treasury Department Thursday, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin presented a set of the newly minted $1 silver and $5 gold coins to his widow, Rachel Robinson.

Robinson was baseball's Rookie of the Year in 1947, when he joined the Dodgers, and played with them until he retired in 1957. He was active in business and politics and in promoting civil rights after his playing career.
Only 200,000 of the commemorative silver coins and 100,000 gold coins are to be minted. The coins were authorised by Congress.

Part of the proceeds from their sale will go to the Jackie Robinson Foundation, which offers educational and leadership programmes for minority youths. If all the coins are sold, the foundation could receive up to $4.5 million, the Treasury estimated.
